source_text: ἐκφωνοῦσιν. Ἀλλὰ ὥσπερ δεινοὶ συκοφάνται καὶ κατήγοροι ἀκρωτηριάσαντες τὸ χωρίον, τὸν ἀγῶνα τῆς κατηγορίας ποιοῦνται.
thought_title: The Arians as mutilating false accusers
orientation: Eustathius continues his accusation that the Arians quote Scripture dishonestly, now describing how they cut up the passage to make their case.
pass_a_gloss: They utter it. But just as clever false accusers and prosecutors, having mutilated (silenced/ torn away) the passage, they make their case for the accusation.

choices.why: δεινός here means skilled or clever in a negative sense, fitting the rhetorical attack on the Arians' method; the glossary requires 'false accusers' for συκοφάνται.
The glossary mandates 'mutilating' for this term; the aorist participle keeps the temporal/causal force of the action preceding the main verb.

choices.english: they make the contest of the accusation
choices.why: ἀγῶνα ποιοῦνται is a middle-voice idiom meaning 'they make/conduct a contest'; keeping 'contest' preserves the forensic metaphor of a legal struggle.
rejected: they wage the battle of accusation

choices.why: χωρίον here refers to a specific scriptural passage, not a physical place; 'passage' is the standard English term for a cited text.

pass_b_english: But like clever false accusers and prosecutors, they mutilate the passage and then stage their contest of accusation.
